# Norman Douglas

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** old reprobate  <sub>[v5 c16 P77](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0077)</sub>

## Appearance

Norman Douglas is a big, fine-looking, red-bearded personage with a massive head and an ungrizzled mane of red hair. He has a high, white, unwrinkled forehead and flashing blue eyes. In his youth, he was known as a handsome, red-haired young giant.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c32 P2](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0002)_

## Personality

Norman Douglas is tempestuous, loud, and inclined to bluster, often compared to a genial whirlwind. He possesses a short, fiery temper, is clever and well read, and enjoys a good argument or lively banter. He dislikes tears or sulking in women, preferring those with spunk and spirit who stand up to him. Though he can be a bully and choleric when irritated, he is generous, genial, and highly appreciative of boldness.

_Sources: [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027), [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P29](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0029), [v5 c16 P55](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0055), [v5 c16 P61](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0061), [v5 c16 P87](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0087), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 c26 P19](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0019), [v5 c26 P21](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0021), [v5 c32 P1](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0001)_

## History

In his youth, Norman Douglas went about with Ellen West for two years. Following a quarrel, he jilted her in a fit of temper and hastily married Hester Reese to spite her. He despised Hester for her meekness, eventually breaking her small spirit, while his refusal to let her contribute to church caused her distress. After a church session member cheated him in a cow deal, Norman stopped attending church for twenty years, living at his farm where he stayed up late reading and frequently squabbled with his housekeeper, Mrs. Wilson. After young Faith Meredith boldly confronted him at his home regarding his absence from church, Norman was so impressed by her spirit that he agreed to return and broke bread with her. Upon seeing Ellen West at church, he fell in love with her again and began pursuing her openly through public courting, bullying, and coaxing. Despite a period of separation and resistance from Ellen, he persisted until they were engaged to be married.

_Sources: [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c15 P38](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0038), [v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027), [v5 c16 P55](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0055), [v5 c16 P60](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0060), [v5 c16 P61](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0061), [v5 c17 P0](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0000), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c33 P5](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0005), [v5 c34 P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)_

## Quotes

> I vow you’ve got spunk, after all—I like spunk. Come, sit down—sit down!  <sub>[v5 c16 P55](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0055)</sub>
